islay.name: Islay
islay.summary: The world's peat benchmark, though the island also makes celebrated unpeated malts.

heavily-peated-malt.serve: Neat or with a few drops of water
heavily-peated-malt.decant: No decanting; rest 5 min in the glass
heavily-peated-malt.expect: Intensely peaty and coastal: bonfire smoke, iodine and sea spray over a firm malt backbone.

style.label: Heavily peated Islay malt · Medicinal & coastal
style.method: Heavily peated barley, pot distilled twice, ex-bourbon casks dominant
style.effect: Peat smoke from barley drying dominates; sea air and oak maturation add brine and sweetness

bottles.name: Laphroaig 10
bottles.note: The medicinal benchmark: iodine, tar and sweet smoke

bottles.name: Ardbeg 10
bottles.note: Bonfire peat balanced by citrus sweetness

bottles.name: Lagavulin 16
bottles.note: Deep, sherry-influenced peat with a long dry finish

unpeated-malt.serve: Neat or with a splash of water
unpeated-malt.expect: Unpeated by Islay's standards: orchard fruit, vanilla cream and a salty coastal edge.

style.label: Unpeated Islay malt · Coastal & fruity
style.effect: Lets the island's maritime character show without smoke; coastal maturation still adds salinity

bottles.name: Bruichladdich The Classic Laddie
bottles.note: Certified unpeated Islay barley, bourbon-cask bright

bottles.name: Bunnahabhain 12
bottles.note: Unpeated and sherry-influenced with coastal weight

identity.setting: Cool maritime island, frequent Atlantic storms
identity.terrain: Low-lying moorland and peat bogs, rocky shores
influences: Peat cut from island bogs for malting

why.cause: Island peat, rich in decayed vegetation and seaweed
why.effect: Burns smoky and medicinal, giving iodine and tar notes

why.cause: Warehouses within reach of Atlantic salt spray
why.effect: Barrels breathe maritime air, adding brine and salinity
Keeps extraction gentle, letting peat character stay prominent

speyside.name: Speyside
speyside.summary: Scotland's sweet heartland: honey and orchard fruit, with celebrated sherry-cask and a few peated expressions.

unpeated-malt.serve: Neat; a drop of water opens the fruit
unpeated-malt.expect: Honeyed and fruity with gentle oak: the approachable face of Scotch.

style.label: Unpeated Speyside malt · Honeyed & fruity
style.method: Unpeated barley, refill ex-bourbon casks, often double distilled
style.effect: Refill bourbon wood keeps the style light, fruity and accessible

bottles.name: Glenfiddich 12
bottles.note: Pear, honey and gentle oak: the beginner's classic

bottles.name: The Balvenie DoubleWood 12
bottles.note: Bourbon casks finished in sherry for layered sweetness

sherry-malt.expect: Rich and sherried: dried fruit, walnut and chocolate with no peat smoke.

style.label: Speyside sherry malt · Rich & sherried
style.method: First-fill and refill sherry casks (European and American oak) over unpeated spirit
style.effect: Sherry wood adds dried fruit, spice and depth; the spirit itself carries no peat

bottles.name: Macallan 12 Sherry Oak
bottles.note: The sherry-cask benchmark: dried fruit and chocolate

bottles.name: Glenfarclas 15
bottles.note: Deep, direct-anchored sherry character

lightly-peated-malt.expect: A gentle wisp of smoke over malt sweetness: Speyside's rarely-peated side.

style.label: Lightly peated Speyside malt · Malt & smoke
style.effect: A trace of peat alongside classic Speyside malt sweetness

bottles.name: Benromach 10
bottles.note: Speyside's peated outlier: delicate smoke over malt and sherry

identity.setting: Sheltered river valley, cool and stable
identity.terrain: Rolling farmland around the River Spey
influences: Over half of Scotland's malt distilleries
Historic access to sherry casks from Spain

why.cause: Sheltered valley with soft river water
why.effect: Gives malts a gentle, honeyed profile
European oak sherry casks impart dried fruit and spice

why.cause: Most Speyside houses do not peat their barley
why.effect: Smoke is the exception here, not the regional signature

highlands.name: Highlands
highlands.climate: Varied: maritime west to continental east
highlands.summary: Scotland's largest region: heather honey in the south, coastal spice in the north, and everything between.

unpeated-malt.expect: Rounded and honeyed with heather and gentle oak: the middle path of Scotch.

style.label: Unpeated Highland malt · Rounded & heathery
style.effect: Heather-honey softness is the common thread across the region's unpeated houses

bottles.name: Dalwhinnie 15
bottles.note: Heather honey and gentle spice from Scotland's highest distillery

bottles.name: Glenmorangie 10 (The Original)
bottles.note: Citrus and vanilla from tall stills and first-fill bourbon casks

lightly-peated-malt.expect: Warm, smouldering Highland peat: earthier and softer than Islay's medicinal smoke.

style.label: Lightly peated Highland malt · Heathery smoke
style.effect: Inland Highland peat reads earthy and heathery rather than medicinal

bottles.name: Ardmore Legacy
bottles.note: Peated Highlander: smouldering, earthy, affordable

identity.setting: Vast region from Atlantic coast to North Sea
influences: Tall stills in the south give lighter spirits
Coastal sites add saline spice in the north and west

why.effect: Coastal, inland and mountain malts all share the Highland name
Peated Highland malts taste earthy and sweet rather than medicinal

lowlands.name: Lowlands
lowlands.summary: Scotland's lightest malts: grassy, floral and often triple-distilled in the Irish tradition.

unpeated-malt.serve: Neat, or as a long highball
unpeated-malt.expect: Light, grassy and delicate: aperitif Scotch with no smoke.

style.label: Unpeated Lowland malt · Light & grassy
style.method: Triple distillation in some houses, unpeated barley, refill casks
style.effect: A third distillation lifts and lightens the spirit

bottles.name: Auchentoshan American Oak
bottles.note: Triple-distilled, bourbon-cask bright and citrusy

bottles.name: Glenkinchie 12
bottles.note: Floral, light and aperitif-friendly

identity.terrain: Low hills and farmland around Edinburgh and Glasgow
influences: Historic triple distillation borrowed from Ireland

why.cause: Triple distillation in the Irish style
why.effect: Removes heavier compounds, giving a lighter, cleaner spirit
Keeps the focus on barley and floral notes

campbeltown.name: Campbeltown
campbeltown.summary: A tiny peninsula enclave: briny, oily malts spanning unpeated to heavily peated.

lightly-peated-malt.expect: Briny, lightly smoky and oily: the classic Campbeltown signature.

style.label: Lightly peated Campbeltown malt · Briny & oily
style.method: Lightly peated barley, 2.5 distillations, ex-bourbon dominant
style.effect: Peninsula sea air and small-still character give a distinct oily brine

bottles.name: Springbank 10
bottles.note: The cult benchmark: briny, oily, lightly smoky

heavily-peated-malt.expect: Campbeltown's peated alter ego: dense bonfire smoke with the peninsula's oily weight.

style.label: Heavily peated Campbeltown malt · Bonfire & brine
style.method: Heavily peated barley, same stills as the house's lightly peated make
style.effect: Peat intensity varies by bottling line even within one distillery

bottles.name: Longrow 10
bottles.note: Springbank's heavily peated line: ash, bonfire and brine

unpeated-malt.expect: Campbeltown without the peat: malty, vanilla-led and still faintly maritime.

style.label: Unpeated Campbeltown malt · Malty & maritime
style.effect: Shows the peninsula's texture with smoke removed

bottles.name: Hazelburn 10
bottles.note: Springbank's unpeated, triple-distilled line

identity.setting: Narrow peninsula on the Kintyre coast
identity.terrain: Small harbor town hemmed by sea
influences: One distillery bottles unpeated, lightly and heavily peated lines

why.cause: Total exposure to sea air on a narrow peninsula
why.effect: Brine and salinity mark even young malts
Oily, characterful spirit that mass production would smooth away

islands.name: Islands
islands.summary: Island malts outside Islay: from Talisker's peppery power to Highland Park's heathered gentleness.

lightly-peated-malt.expect: Gentle heathery smoke with honeyed fruit: the Orkney island style.

style.label: Lightly peated island malt · Heathered & honeyed
style.method: Lightly peated barley (around 15 ppm or less), sherry and ex-bourbon casks
style.effect: Orkney's heather peat reads floral and honeyed rather than medicinal

bottles.name: Highland Park 12
bottles.note: Heather honey and gentle, subtle smoke from Orkney

peated-malt.serve: Neat with a splash of water
peated-malt.expect: Powerful peppery smoke and brine: Skye's storm-driven signature.

style.label: Peated island malt · Peppery & maritime
style.method: Fully peated barley, ex-bourbon and sherry casks, tall-necked stills
style.effect: Skye's exposed maturation intensifies pepper and smoke together

bottles.name: Talisker 10
bottles.note: Peppery, powerful peat smoke and sea spray from Skye

identity.terrain: Rocky coastlines, sea cliffs, heather moorland
influences: Every warehouse sits within sight of the sea
Each island has its own peat character

why.effect: Salt and pepper notes appear across the family

why.cause: Local heather-rich peat in the north
why.effect: Softer, honeyed smoke rather than medicinal Islay peat
